jobs.title: Applied ML Engineer/Data Scientist
jobs.jd: 🍇 About grape: Our entrepreneurial spirit drives us in what we do and what we are passionate about. Our mission is to become the premier health partner in the insurance business. Recognising the need for innovation in the traditional employee insurance model we are set to revolutionize the employee insurance industry. We help companies support people before and after they get sick and to make more of their time. Our insurance solutions reduce monotonous and manual work for employees, doctors, HR & payroll managers. As we strive to lead a technology-driven transformation, we put employees first. At grape we pride ourselves on our people and our culture. We continue to grow fast and that’s where you come in. Our team is dynamic, diverse and full of creative ideas. Want to join? We can’t wait to get to know you! Your role Our data and tech give us an edge in risk assessment, pricing and premium calculation. This role turns that into accurate models that support our carrier partners and our growth, builds tuned models where they beat rules and off-the-shelf LLMs in claims (triage, intervention, return-to-work, fraud), and responsibly explores how data can help employees stay healthy through grape Care. We’re looking for an applied ML engineer / data scientist to build predictive models from the ground up on real, regulated insurance data. You’ll own problems end to end, from effective-dated records to production, in a domain where correctness and responsible use genuinely matter. Starting points include pricing and risk, portfolio monitoring, claims and payment patterns, triage and return-to-work, absence, and fraud detection. grape sits on a rich dataset, though, and you’ll help find the next high-value use cases. You’re candid about what the data can support, and you propose simpler approaches when they’re the right answer. This is not an LLM role. LLM and agent workflows and document extraction sit with our engineering teams, and you’ll use their outputs as features. What you'll do: Build and validate models Own the full model lifecycle: feature engineering, training, evaluation, explainability, deployment, and drift monitoring. Backtest on the historical book and run models in shadow mode alongside human decision-makers, reporting where and why they disagree. Produce audit-ready validation and governance documentation that actuarial, compliance, and carrier partners can review. Platform and MLOps Deploy models on grape’s cloud platform within strict security and data-residency requirements for health data. Set up experiment tracking, model versioning, and production monitoring, partnering with engineering on integration. Shape the problem space Identify and prioritize high-value use cases as you explore the dataset, rather than waiting to be handed problems. Turn ambiguous business questions into well-defined, measurable modelling. Responsible & explainable by design Build privacy, fairness, and explainability into every model that touches personal or health data, working with compliance and legal on nDSG/GDPR boundaries. Models support decisions; accountable owners make them. Pricing, reserving, and claims work requires licensed-actuary sign-off, and any automation requires governance approval first. Collaborate Explain model behavior and limits to underwriting, claims, actuarial, and compliance teams. What you'll need: Strong applied ML and statistics: supervised and unsupervised learning, anomaly detection, time-series, and survival/duration modeling. Proven experience building models on real-world, relational, effective-dated data, including imbalanced outcomes. Fluent Python (pandas, scikit-learn, a modern ML stack) and strong SQL. Solid grasp of validation, calibration, and explainability (e.g. SHAP). Production MLOps: experiment tracking, versioning, and drift monitoring. Sound judgment on data privacy and modelling. Fluent English. Bias for action, ownership, and clear cross-functional communication. Big plus: Insurance, actuarial, or risk modeling (pricing, reserving, loss ratios). Health, disability, or absence data, especially Swiss insurance (KTG, UVG); fraud detection in claims. Regulated special-category data under nDSG/GDPR, or model risk management. Google Cloud, including security-restricted deployments. German language skills. 🤝 What we offer in return: 🌱 Empowering workplace: Join a passionate team and an empowering workplace where you are given the ownership, tools, and support to make decisions and take initiative. Together we grow and build innovative solutions. 💻 Hybrid setup: Enjoy the flexibility of our hybrid work schedule, with the freedom to work remotely or from our office in Zurich. On Thursdays, our team day, we meet together in our Zurich office. 🪑 Home office stipend: To enable our hybrid setup, we allocate a one-off CHF 200.- home office budget to help you set up your dream workspace in the comfort of your own home. 🌐 Internet allowance: We give you a monthly internet allowance to help cover your internet costs at home and enable you to work seamlessly from your home office. ⏳ Flexible working time: You can distribute your working hours the way you want to. 🧠 Learning budget: We support you in improving your skills, acquiring new knowledge and advancing your career. We also allocate a CHF 1'500.- budget annually ❤️‍🩹 Well-being: Work-life balance is important to us and we foster a supportive work environment. We support you with mental health sessions with our partner Aepsy. 🎫 Team events: Every month we gather for fun and engaging events where we can connect and bond with our colleagues and our teams. ✈️ Team retreats: Once a year we travel somewhere nice to bond with our colleagues. 🚂 Travel and commute: We will cover your SBB half fare card, so we can spend some time together in the office. 🌴 Paid vacation: You get 5 weeks (25 days) of paid vacation every year and 2 additional days of paid vacation to compensate for canton-related holidays, religious

jobs.title: Senior Backend & AI Engineer (Remote)
jobs.jd: This role is open only to candidates living in the EU or EEA. We can't consider applications from other locations. If you've built something before, start here The hardest part of a startup usually isn't the code. It's finding customers who really need what you build and getting them to change how they work. At Scalera, that part is done: manufacturers, suppliers and contractors across Switzerland, Austria and Germany already run their tenders through us every day. What we need now are people who can take the next unsolved problem and turn it into a product customers can't do without. If you've founded a company (whether it worked out or not), been the first engineer somewhere, or built something people paid for, this role was written for you. About Scalera Scalera is an ETH Zurich spin-off building AI for the €200B+ European construction industry. Large manufacturers and suppliers still run their most document-heavy processes by hand, from reading 300-page tenders to retyping purchase orders into their ERP. We automate them one by one. Our product matching already handles 1,400 tender positions in 16 minutes at 98% precision, work that used to take a sales rep most of a day. What you'll do You'll be part product manager, part engineer. You'll spend real time with customers and help shape what we build. Sometimes you'll spot the next problem yourself, and sometimes we'll hand you a clear priority to run with. Spend real time with customers. Join calls and site visits, sit with the people who do the work, and understand why they do it the way they do. You'll know their problems firsthand, not from a ticket. Shape what to build. Turn what you hear into a clear problem, a scope and a plan, and push back when the obvious request isn't the real need. When we bring you a priority, you'll own how it gets solved. Build it. Design and build backend services in Go and Python that turn messy tenders, catalogs and purchase orders into data customers can rely on. Ship, then check. Get it in front of customers fast, watch how they actually use it, and iterate. Own it in production. When something breaks at a customer, it's yours to understand and fix. Build with AI. Use AI heavily in how you work, and design systems that agents can use as well as people. What success looks like after 3 months There's a part of the product people now think of as yours, and you're the one deciding what happens to it next You've spotted a problem nobody asked you to solve, made the case for it, and shipped a first version You've shipped features from both sources: priorities we set and ideas from your own customer conversations At least once, you've talked us out of building something customers didn't really need You've left a part of the platform simpler than you found it You'll probably thrive here if You've taken something from zero to one: a company, a product line, or a side project with paying users You've built and run backend systems in production that other people depend on. We care more about your judgment than your language; you're strong in Go or Python and happy to work in both You're solid on data modeling, API design and messy real-world data You'd rather talk to a customer than wait for a spec You're comfortable with ambiguity. You can make progress while the problem is still half-defined, which at a startup it usually is You want a large scope of responsibility and are happy to own things well beyond your job title Rapidly changing requirements don't throw you. When customers or priorities shift, you adapt and keep going You enjoy direct customer contact and want to be on customer calls You make things simpler over time, not more clever You write clearly in English. German is a plus, not a requirement You probably won't enjoy it if You just want to code and go home You don't like talking to customers, whether on calls or on the occasional site visit Ambiguity and chaos bother you You want a well-defined backlog handed to you Your main goal is managing people soon. Here, scope grows with what you own, not with headcount Our stack Go and Python (FastAPI), PostgreSQL, GCP, and LLMs throughout the document pipeline. You don't need to know all of it on day one. How we hire Screening call (30 min) with our VP Engineering. It's two-way: ask us anything, including the hard questions. Technical deep-dive call : walk us through something you built from scratch, the decisions you made and what went wrong. Meet Scalera Day : join us remotely to work on a real problem with real (anonymized) construction documents, and meet the team. Offer : if it's a fit on both sides, we'll move quickly to an offer. Working at Scalera Remote within the EU or EEA Small team, no bureaucracy. You'll work directly with the CEO, CTO, VP Engineering and Customer Success Competitive compensation Founders and former founders: if you're unsure whether you fit, send a few lines about what you built and why you moved on. We read every one. Find more English Speaking Jobs in Switzerland on Arbeitnow

Your work will directly impact the performance, scalability, and ethical alignment of our cutting-edge LLMs and AI agents, enabling businesses to unlock unprecedented levels of productivity and innovation with AI that is truly grounded in their data. Proficiency in Python and experience with relevant AI/ML frameworks such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, or JAX. A strong foundation in machine learning principles, deep learning architectures, and natural language processing, particularly with large language models. Experience with cloud platforms (e.g., AWS, GCP, Azure) and MLOps tools for managing the AI lifecycle. Demonstrated ability to write clean, efficient, and well-tested code for scalable software systems. Exceptional problem-solving skills and a passion for tackling complex technical challenges with creative AI solutions. You Connect by collaborating seamlessly across diverse teams, Challenge the status quo to innovate, and Own your projects with a commitment to impact and excellence. 🍩 Benefits & perks (UK full-time employees): Generous PTO, plus company holidays Comprehensive medical and dental insurance Paid parental leave for all parents (16 weeks) Fertility and family planning support Competitive pension scheme and company contribution Annual work-life stipends for: Wellness stipend for gym, massage/chiropractor, personal training, etc. Learning and development stipend Company-wide off-sites and team off-sites Competitive compensation and company stock options Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

jobs.jd: This role is also open to candidates living in the EU or EEA. We can't consider applications from other locations. If you've built something before, start here Most ML jobs hand you a benchmark. This one hands you a business problem with paying customers and their real data. Construction tenders are long, messy and full of trade jargon, and every decision a customer makes on our platform becomes a labeled example you can train on. We need someone who can turn that data into models that customers notice: from the first experiment to the model serving production traffic, and back again when a customer says it got something wrong. If you've founded a company (whether it worked out or not), been the first ML engineer somewhere, or shipped a model people paid for, this role was written for you. About Scalera Scalera is an ETH Zurich spin-off building AI for the €200B+ European construction industry. Manufacturers, wholesalers and suppliers in Switzerland, Austria and Germany still run their most document-heavy work by hand, from reading 300-page tenders to retyping purchase orders into their ERP. We automate that work one process at a time, and ML sits at the center of every one of them. What you'll own You'll own the ML behind our products, end to end. In practice that means: Training and fine-tuning : embedding models, rerankers, classifiers and LLMs, trained on our own data. Document understanding : models that pull structure, quantities and product specs out of tenders, orders and catalogs. Product matching : retrieval and LLM agents that match tender positions to the right products. Evaluation : offline benchmarks, per-customer evals and gates that keep a new model from shipping if it makes things worse. Training and serving infrastructure : automated retrain pipelines, GPU serving and vector search in production. Customer problems : when a model gets something wrong for a customer, finding out why and fixing it. What success looks like after 3 months There's a model or part of the pipeline people now think of as yours, and you're the one deciding what happens to it next. You've spotted a problem nobody asked you to solve, made the case for it, and shipped a first version. A model you trained runs in production, and customers can see the difference in their results. Retraining runs automatically, and nothing reaches customers without passing an eval you designed. You've cut LLM cost or latency by replacing an expensive step with a smaller model of your own. You've decided at least one thing we should stop building. You'll probably thrive here if You've taken something from zero to one: a company, a model in production, or a side project with real users. You've trained and fine-tuned models yourself, ideally embeddings, retrieval or document models, and evaluated them honestly on held-out data. You've built with LLMs in production and know where agents fail. You write strong Python and can run what you build: Docker, CI/CD, and cloud on GCP, AWS or Azure. You measure before you believe, and a single aggregate score doesn't convince you. You'd rather open a customer's actual document than wait for a spec. You're comfortable with ambiguity. You can make progress while the problem is still half-defined, which at a startup it usually is. You want a large scope of responsibility and are happy to own things well beyond your job title. Rapidly changing requirements don't throw you. When customers or priorities shift, you adapt and keep going. You enjoy direct customer contact and want to be on customer calls. You write clearly in English. German is a plus, not a requirement. You probably won't enjoy it if You just want to code and go home. You don't like talking to customers. Ambiguity and chaos bother you. You want a well-defined research agenda handed to you. You'd rather hand a model to someone else to deploy and debug. Your main goal is managing people soon. Here, scope grows with what you own, not with headcount. Our stack Python and PyTorch, open-weight and frontier LLMs, LangGraph, Langfuse, PostgreSQL with pgvector, Pinecone, and GCP. You don't need to know all of it on day one. How we hire Screening call (30 min) with our VP Engineering. It's two-way: ask us anything, including the hard questions. Technical deep-dive call : walk us through a model or system you built, the decisions you made and what went wrong in production. Meet Scalera Day : come to our office in Zürich, work on a real problem with real (anonymized) tender data, and meet the team. Offer : if it's a fit on both sides, we'll move quickly to an offer. jobs.title: Forward Deployed Engineer
jobs.jd: Your Impact Procurement is over 50% of revenue for industrial companies and their biggest lever for profitability. The hard part isn't the software. Every customer's reality is different: a different ERP, a different data model, decades of undocumented process. Generic platforms stall exactly there, and that's where most enterprise AI value quietly dies. At Tacto, the people who close that gap are Builders who work at the customer edge. You sit inside the customer's environment, build in their production data, and turn what you learn there into product. More than 300 industrial companies already run on Tacto, and every new one teaches us something the platform should do on its own. Your Tasks Prove it with their data. Show a prospect or customer what Tacto finds in their own spend, suppliers and parts, fast enough that the value is obvious. Build in customer environments. Data pipelines, agents and custom logic on top of the Tacto platform, in real production data, until the procurement team can actually work with the result. Be in the room, on site. Run workshops with buyers and key users, debug alongside their IT, and see how a company really buys instead of how the process documentation says it buys. Turn the edge into product. When you solve something twice, ship it into the platform so nobody has to solve it a third time. You're done when it drives revenue, not when the deployment is live. Automate your own job. If a step can be done by an agent, you build the agent and prove it works. Your Profile You've built something people relied on: software, automations, agents, or a technical project that real users used. You build with AI every day. Cursor, Claude, Codex and agents are your default, and you've built with LLMs against real, messy data. You're hands-on with data. SQL and Python at working level, or the drive to get there fast with AI as leverage. You thrive in messy environments. Incomplete requirements, undocumented data and conflicting stakeholders don't stop you. You earn customer trust. You explain technical decisions clearly, handle pushback, and don't over-promise. Early in your career? Good. We bet on people with a steep learning curve, and our senior Builders spend real time making others faster. Native-level German and fluent English, based in Munich, happy to travel across DACH. What This Role Is, and Isn't We want to be honest about what you are signing up for. This is not an engineering role with customers kept at a safe distance. Customer contact is the job, not a tax on the job. If you want a ticket queue and clean requirements, this is the wrong role. This is not consulting. Nobody here bills days. You are measured on what the customer can do afterwards and on what made it into the platform. It is deliberately broad. If you want to specialise narrowly you will be frustrated here. The deal: prove yourself, deliver real impact, make a strong case for yourself, then we back your next step in every way we can. How the process works Say Hello (20 min): get to know each other and the role Hiring Manager Interview (45 min) On-site day: a case with three Builders and Pool Leads (1 hour), Meet the Team (30 min) Our Background Tacto is building the intelligence layer that connects AI to the physical world of manufacturing, starting with procurement. AI is transforming every industry, but it stops at the factory gate. The knowledge that holds manufacturing together - part costs, suppliers, materials - is scattered across systems and people. Over 50% of a product's cost originates from suppliers, making procurement the single largest cost lever in manufacturing and the missing connection between the digital and the physical world. Yet it still runs on Excel and legacy systems. We're changing that with our Procurement Intelligence Platform, trusted by hundreds of companies running billions of Euros of material. Based in Munich, we are 100+ passionate builders who are in-office, with high expectations, fast growth, and a lot of fun. We are supported by >€50m from Sequoia, Index, and Europe's leading tech entrepreneurs and industry veterans. Why It Matters Manufacturing forms Europe's economic backbone, driving a fourth of Europe's GDP and providing over 30% of jobs. These hidden champions and global market leaders manufacture the physical world around us, from the machines that build our cities to the medical devices that save lives. But the world is changing. The US dominates the digital world of bits. China is scaling the world of atoms, manufacturing at unprecedented speed and scale. Geopolitics are more uncertain than ever. Europe's strength lies in its deep industrial knowledge through generations of engineering. Manufacturing worldwide runs on European machines and software. But that heritage is only an advantage if we leverage it in the age of AI. Tacto builds the AI that connects Atoms and Bits, empowering our Industrial Base to Stay Stronger and building a lighthouse for European tech. What We Offer The people at Tacto are passionate about building the organization, growing themselves, and our product while having fun and being real. We have high expectations, great talent density, and a culture where your ambition, performance, and agency are what count - not where you come from or how big your ego is. You'll grow at the forefront of AI, have real ownership and impact, and be surrounded by the best people in their field who challenge you and make you better every day. That is demanding and rewarding, but that's where we thrive. Besides that you have: Money: Competitive salary & equity in the company with real upside, so you are invested in our success Workplace: A vibrant in-office culture (> 4 days/week) in a beautiful office in central Munich Development: A development budget and regular exposure to exceptional people, e.g., Lunch & Learns, peer mentoring, external speakers Time off: 26 + 4 vacation days per year (4 fixed “company rest days”) as well as regular o

jobs.title: AI Engineer
jobs.jd: About us People assume the supply chain is an automated, algorithmic system. It is not. It is a large number of people acting as the glue between organisations and systems, doing work the world depends on with tools that have barely changed in decades. Nexcade builds AI agents for those people, starting in freight forwarding, a $210BN industry. Our agents are live in production with some of the leading global forwarders, pricing millions in freight every week, and we are expanding the platform deeper into the shipment lifecycle. We have raised $8.5M to make this a reality. Our founders, Dan and Tasho, spent years at Sedna and Palantir working with supply chain companies on problems like this one. We are backed by top VCs and angels who backed or founded Synthesia, n8n and other world-class companies. How we work Everybody codes, founders included. The whole company is technical, commercial team included, and runs on coding agents. Closely with customers and design partners, so what we ship changes how they operate. At pace. Fast cycles and quick iterations, on the product and on how we work. End to end. If you see something broken or missing, you have the freedom (and the responsibility) to fix it. In person, 4+ days a week in London. We value synchronous communication. Debate rigorously, decide quickly, execute relentlessly. Enjoy the journey. Hard problems, good colleagues. The role We are building the AI platform for freight forwarding and expanding our product surface, and we are hiring software engineers across product, AI and platform to do it. You will build products that do freight forwarding work alongside our customers' teams, operating across the entire shipment lifecycle. You will work across the stack in Python, TypeScript and React, and directly with customers and founders on what gets built. Everyone here works across the stack, but each engineer has a spike: the area where they set the bar for the team. You spend most of your time where yours is, and lean on your colleagues where theirs are. Product: You build best in class products for the core jobs in freight forwarding, one job at a time. You work as a design partner with our customers to understand the work deeply, turn that understanding into a product they would choose over anything else, and feed what you learn back into the platform everyone builds on. AI: You raise the ceiling on what our AI can do and the floor on how reliably it does it. That spans high volume tasks like classification and extraction and deep workflow tasks that run for hours. You design for performance, reliability, explainability and control, set up the gyms and evals to measure them, and build the harness that runs our agents in all of our products. Platform: You own the foundation every product stands on: the runtime for thousands of concurrent agents and workflows, the way they communicate and scale, the controls for how they access data with permissions that hold, and the observability to see and measure all of it. You ensure the rest of the team can move fast without fear. What we look for A spike, with evidence. Something you have been exceptional at and proof of it. We hire on slope rather than years, so there is no experience threshold in either direction. Strong fundamentals. In the AI-assisted era, having good technical judgement is key. You have shipped production systems people depend on, seen them fail and learned from it. High agency and ownership. You take an ambiguous problem, make a call, and see it through. Humility and learning velocity. You want to get better and you change your mind when the evidence says so. Interest in the problem. You do not need a freight background, but you need to find messy real-world operations interesting rather than a chore. Why join You will shape the product, the architecture and the company, working alongside an engineering team from Palantir, Raft, Faculty, UnlikelyAI and Oxford. You will work directly with the businesses using what you build, on AI applied to an industry that has resisted software for decades. You will get meaningful equity, so when this works you share in it. Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

jobs.jd: About Us Legora is redefining how legal work gets done. Not built for lawyers, built with them. We work alongside the world’s best legal teams, who expect excellence, precision, and speed, and we hold ourselves to the same bar. Our AI-native workspace lets legal professionals move faster, think more clearly, and operate with sharper precision. By analysing thousands of documents in minutes and powering end-to-end workflows, we cut through complexity, teams can focus on what matters: judgment, strategy, and outcomes. 2,100+ customers across 80+ countries trust us, including Cleary Gottlieb, Goodwin, Linklaters, White & Case, Dentons, and Barclays. We’ve scaled to $200M+ in ARR , with teams across Europe, North America and APAC, and continue to expand through acquisitions including Qura, Walter AI, Graceview, Cadastral, and Wexler. We partner with world-class performers: including Aaron Judge and the New York Yankees, Ludvig Åberg (and his caddie), and campaigns featuring Jude Law. Joining Legora means three things. We lean in: ownership over titles, outcomes over intentions. We fight for excellence: high standards, direct, ego-free feedback. We grow together: as a team and with our customers. Mission before ego. Everyone contributes. No one coasts. If you’re driven by impact, pace, and raising the bar. This is the place. What you'll do Legal AI is inventing its best practices in real time, and this role sits where that happens. You'll sit within the Legal Engineering team and work hand in hand with Product at one of the fastest-growing legal AI companies in the world, seeing new capabilities before almost anyone else, experimenting with them against real legal work, and turning what you learn into the standards a global function runs on. In a year here, you will see and vet more legal AI use cases than most people in the industry see in a career, working directly with some of the best legal engineers in the industry. This is a judgement role, not a filing one. You'll be the person who vets the skills, workflows and use cases the function ships: testing them hands-on, separating the genuinely strong from the merely plausible, and quality-controlling practice-area workflows so that what carries the Legora name is consistently excellent. You'll research and experiment with prompting techniques and applied AI methods, author the exemplar use cases the rest of the function copies, and teach what you learn: delivering technical onboarding for new Legal Engineers in your region and broadcasting best practices to the team worldwide. And because judgement needs grounding, around 30% of your time stays on live client work, chosen for what it teaches. Specifically, you will • Vet the Skills Library and Legal Engineering outputs against the quality bar: review skills, workflows and use cases hands-on before they go live, and quality-control practice-area workflows for consistency. • Research and experiment with prompting techniques, skill patterns and emerging AI methods, and turn what works into best practices the whole function adopts. • Author the reference use cases that show what great looks like, published as the exemplars others copy. • Work closely with the Product team on up-and-coming capabilities: early hands-on testing, the first best practices for new features, and structured feedback from real use. • Produce materials that would support the technical onboarding and training for new Legal Engineers in your region, such as best practices to create use cases etc. • Communicate new best practices, exemplars and platform changes to the Legal Engineering team worldwide. • Support the flagship demos our CEO and C-suite take on stage at the industry’s biggest events: use case preparation, fixtures and rehearsal support. • Oversee the quality and currency of the use case and skills libraries, including coordination across regions • Spend roughly 30% of your time on live client work, selected for what it feeds back into the standards and libraries. What you bring You're a lawyer with real practice experience who has become genuinely technical: maybe you did a coding bootcamp, maybe you taught yourself, but either way you're the person colleagues ask how something actually works. You live in AI tools, and it shows: you can tell a strong use case from a plausible-sounding weak one, you know why a prompt underperforms before you've finished reading it, and you hold both halves of the judgement this role needs: what makes a prompt run well, and what makes a legal output substantively right rather than merely fluent. When you vet, you vet properly: line by line against the source, with the discipline to put the AI down when the job calls for your own eyes. jobs.title: Data Scientist, FX Quantitative Research
jobs.jd:
Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world's largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

Data Science at Stripe is a vibrant community where data scientists and data analysts learn and grow together. The Treasury Finance Data Science team builds the models, risk frameworks, and decision tools behind how Stripe manages money at global scale: liquidity, funding, counterparty risk, and foreign exchange.

Stripe moves funds across 135+ currencies every day. That creates FX exposure from merchant flows, multi-currency balances, and entity funding. In this role, you'll be a thought partner and builder alongside Stripe's FX team. Together you'll develop the quantitative foundation for how Stripe measures, forecasts, and hedges FX exposure.

What you'll do

You'll be the senior quantitative lead for FX within Treasury Finance Data Science. You'll co-build with Treasury, the FX hedging team, Finance, and Engineering: shaping the research agenda, turning ideas into rigorous models, and building the systems that put those models to work. Data Science owns these systems. They produce the decision-critical outputs and analyses that the FX team and Treasury leadership rely on. This is a hands-on role. You'll design the methodology, write the code, and ship it into production.

Responsibilities

  • Partner with the FX team to build and evolve FX risk measurement: exposure aggregation across entities and currencies, VaR / Expected Shortfall, stress testing, and scenario analysis
  • Develop forecasting models for FX exposures and multi-currency cash flows. Quantify forecast uncertainty so it can inform hedge sizing and timing.
  • Co-design hedge optimization and decision frameworks with the FX team that weigh hedge cost, residual risk, P&L volatility, and liquidity constraints
  • Build ML and statistical systems for trading and risk (signal research, anomaly detection on flows, execution and cost analytics), and take them from prototype to production
  • Own the production systems that generate decision-critical FX outputs, partnering with Engineering on reliability, SLAs, monitoring, alerting, and incident response for risk-critical workflows
  • Partner deeply with Treasury Finance stakeholders to turn business questions into quantitative frameworks. Anticipate needs and help shape FX risk strategy rather than reacting to requests.
  • Produce clear, trusted analyses and reporting that inform Treasury and Finance leadership decisions, including leadership-level reporting such as MBRs and QBRs
  • Use AI tools (code assistants, LLM-based agents) to speed up modeling, analysis, and automation, while maintaining rigor, validation, and auditability
  • Raise the technical bar for FX quantitative work within Data Science: methodology standards, model validation, documentation, and mentoring other data scientists

Who you are

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Location Requirement

  • New York, NY required (50% in office - hybrid)

Minimum requirements

  • PhD with 1-3 years, MS or MA with 2-6 years, or BS or BA with 4-8 years of data science or quantitative modeling experience
  • Hands-on quantitative experience at a bank, asset manager, hedge fund, trading firm, or similar financial institution, with direct exposure to FX, rates, or market risk
  • Strong foundation in statistics, probability, and time-series modeling, plus working knowledge of risk measures (VaR, Expected Shortfall, stress testing) and hedging instruments (forwards, swaps, options)
  • Proficiency in Python and SQL. You write production-quality code, not just research scripts.
  • Experience taking models or analytical systems from research into production
  • Business acumen and the ability to turn complex analyses into clear, decision-ready insights
  • Ability to clearly communicate results and drive impact with cross-functional partners, including senior non-technical stakeholders
  • Ability to manage multiple projects at once, with strong attention to detail
  • Experience using AI tools to speed up modeling, analysis, and coding

Preferred qualifications

  • Degree in a quantitative field (e.g., Quantitative / Mathematical Finance, Financial Engineering, Statistics, Mathematics, Physics, Computer Science, Economics, Operations Research)
  • Applied machine learning experience in trading or risk (e.g., forecasting, execution analytics, signal research, anomaly detection)
  • Experience with corporate treasury or balance-sheet FX: multi-entity exposure management, hedge programs, and treasury concepts such as liquidity, funding, and cash positioning
  • Experience building risk or decision systems with engineering standards: code review, testing, monitoring, and defined SLAs
  • Experience with distributed data tools (e.g., Spark) and workflow orchestration (e.g., Airflow, Flyte)

jobs.title: Founding ML Engineer (Spectrum)
jobs.jd:
Software engineers and AI agents alike suffer from the same problem: finding that one person or place that will answer their tough, specific question. Many solutions promise to solve this with similarity search in vector databases. Unfortunately, finding the answer is often a puzzle with pieces to be collected across a myriad of contradictory sources and cannot be solved without surgical search and careful reasoning. 

Spectrum collects data from an organization’s code, docs, and issues, and organizes knowledge in a unified ontology that AI agents can efficiently search through and reason over. We aim to revolutionize the semantic layer space for software-building organizations and move beyond specs that fall out of sync with code, introducing a living spec – one that’s extracted from the whole system and used to keep it aligned. Spectrum is meant to be the single source of truth for all product and architectural knowledge.

Spectrum is a resident of JetBrains' startup incubator, with startup speed and autonomy, and backed by 25 years of developer tooling expertise. We are looking for a top-class ML Engineer who will help us shape the future of software development. You will own our AI and ML engineering stack and help define the research agenda for our team. Your technical vision and design decisions will directly shape the product and determine its success.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Designing and building the ML/LLM solution for data ingestion, knowledge extraction, retrieval, and subsequent reasoning.
  • Creating the datasets, metrics, and pipelines that drive measurable improvements across the system.
  • Architecting and improving agents for context retrieval, knowledge extraction, and data alignment, which includes prompt engineering, model selection, and inference optimization.
  • Establishing MLOps practices, including orchestration, observability, and experiment tracking.
  • Collaborating with the engineering team on system design and with JetBrains Research on the research agenda.
  • Defining hiring criteria, growing the ML team, and shaping the ML team culture.

We expect you to have:

  • A proven track record as an ML/AI Lead.
  • At least five years of experience in ML/AI systems, with at least two years focused on LLMs and generative AI.
  • A deep understanding of the LLM ecosystem, including model architectures and fine-tuning approaches.
  • Hands-on experience with:
    • Prompt engineering and LLM pipeline design, including evaluation.
    • Agentic frameworks such as LangChain, LlamaIndex, LangSmith, smolagents, or an equivalent.
    • Vector databases and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) patterns.
    • Deploying and scaling LLM-powered applications using APIs (e.g. OpenAI or Anthropic) or open-source models.
  • Strong Python skills – Kotlin knowledge would be a plus.
  • Excellent communication skills, with the ability to explain complex technical concepts to diverse audiences.
  • Proficiency in English, both written and verbal. 

Our ideal candidate would have:

  • Experience with ontologies, knowledge graphs, or graph-based reasoning.
  • Experience in early-stage startups – you enjoy the zero-to-one phase.
  • The ability to think strategically about product-led AI, beyond just training models in isolation.
  • A background in code analysis, developer tools, or software engineering research.
  • Experience with multi-agent systems or complex agentic workflows.
  • Actively contributed to relevant open-source projects or publications.

What we offer

  • A competitive salary and JetBrains benefits.
  • A generous runway and corporate resources with startup autonomy.

jobs.title: LLM Fine-Tuning Engineer
jobs.jd: Cos'è Blox Space ? Blox Space lavora al centro dell'economia tech,in partnership con un network di oltre 70 realtà attive nel mondo dell'AI, del software, della cybersecurity e delle Freedom Technologies, impegnate nello sviluppo di infrastrutture, prodotti e servizi legati all'economia digitale, alla data protection e al futuro del denaro. ﻿Aiutiamo a connettere i talenti con questo ecosistema, operando come Talent Bridge tra le ambizioni di crescita dei professionisti e le opportunità offerte dal nostro network. ﻿In questo momento stiamo supportando una delle nostre partner companies nella ricerca di un LLM Fine-Tuning Engineer, e se pensi di essere il profilo giusto, ci piacerebbe conoscerti. Il Ruolo L'azienda è una startup di cybersecurity italiana che costruisce sistemi di sicurezza autonomi: individuano vulnerabilità sconosciute, prioritizzano il rischio reale e distribuiscono le correzioni senza intervento umano, con un focus sui binari compilati, perché è quello che gira davvero in produzione. È un team early, pre-seed, fondato da ricercatori di sicurezza e accademici di primo piano. ﻿Cerchiamo un LLM Fine-Tuning Engineer che adatti, valuti e metta in produzione modelli linguistici open-weight, ma piegati a un unico scopo: trovare e capire vulnerabilità. Per questo cerchiamo una persona fortemente orientata alla cybersecurity, che non si limiti ad addestrare modelli ma capisca il dominio su cui lavorano. Non è un ruolo di prompt engineering: è l'intero ciclo di post-training, dal design dei dataset al fine tuning, dalla generazione di dati sintetici alla valutazione, fino al deploy in ambienti locali, privati o ristretti. ﻿ Non cerchiamo il curriculum perfetto, cerchiamo la testa giusta. Cerchiamo chi sa trasformare un foundation model in un sistema affidabile e specifico per il compito, sa quando il fine tuning è la strada giusta e quando invece conviene prompting, retrieval, orchestrazione o tooling, e porta con sé una vera sensibilità per il mindset di chi attacca. ﻿ Le responsabilità di un LLM Fine-Tuning Engineer in questo contesto possono spaziare dal fine tuning e dall'adattamento di LLM open-weight per casi d'uso di sicurezza, interni o rivolti al cliente, al confronto tra approcci di post-training (SFT, tecniche parameter-efficient come LoRA e QLoRA, preference tuning come DPO dove serve, full fine tuning quando giustificato), dalla costruzione e pulizia di dataset di qualità e dalla generazione di dati sintetici alla definizione di metodi di valutazione che vanno oltre i benchmark generici, fino all'analisi di regressioni e failure mode e al lavoro con il team di engineering per servire i modelli in ambienti vincolati. ﻿﻿﻿ Le skill che fanno la differenza Esperienza pratica vera nel fine tuning di LLM: in produzione, in ricerca applicata o in contesti sperimentali seri, con più tecniche di post-training alle spalle, idealmente SFT, LoRA e QLoRA. Orientamento forte alla cybersecurity: capisci (o hai una gran voglia di capire a fondo) threat model, bug hunting e la logica di chi attacca. È il dominio su cui i modelli lavorano, e qui fa la differenza tra un buon fine tuning e uno inutile. Dati prima di tutto: sai costruire, curare e mantenere dataset per training e valutazione, e sai generare, filtrare e validare dati sintetici per migliorare il comportamento del modello, non per gonfiare le metriche. Stack solido: Python forte, PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, tokenizzazione, preprocessing e training pipeline sono pane quotidiano. Dimestichezza con i vincoli reali: limiti di GPU, trade-off memoria/performance, workflow quantization-aware e ottimizzazione del training. Mentalità da debugging: sai capire perché un modello è migliorato, è regredito, ha fatto overfit o ha fallito, e la valutazione la imposti su quello che conta davvero a livello operativo, non sui punteggi generici. Autonomia a cavallo tra ricerca, dati ed engineering: ti muovi da solo su tutti e tre i fronti. Sono Very Nice to Have: un background in software security o vulnerability research, esperienza in CTF, deploy in ambienti air-gapped, on-premise o ristretti, inference optimization, quantization, model serving o runtime LLM locali, training distribuito o multi-GPU, eval harness, red-teaming o model safety testing. Ti manca qualcosa rispetto a quello che hai letto? Candidati comunque: siamo a caccia di game-changer, non di checklist da spuntare!﻿ Work arrangements Il ruolo ha come sede preferenziale l'hub di Blox Space a Torino, un ambiente cost-effective e ad alta densità di persone tecniche di valore, ma valutiamo candidature da tutta Italia, con modalità operative flessibili da concordare insieme al team. ﻿Per il ruolo è previsto un range retributivo di 40.000 – 60.000 € lordi annui, con la disponibilità a valutare anche proposte superiori per profili particolarmente senior o di valore eccezionale. ﻿Sono inoltre previsti un contributo di 1.000 € per il setup dell'home office, un piano AI premium a tua scelta e retreat aziendali in Italia. Unisciti all'ecosistema con Blox Space ! Se vuoi rendere i modelli open-weight davvero affidabili e utili contro uno dei problemi più difficili della sicurezza, e farlo accanto a chi trova bug veri in sistemi veri, questa è l'opportunità che stavi aspettando: lavorare con una delle nostre partner companies significa entrare in un team innovativo e in forte crescita, al centro di un ecosistema dove circolano idee, competenze e progetti ad alta intensità. È un ambiente dove si costruisce, si testa, si discute e si migliora ogni giorno. Originally posted on Himalayas

jobs.jd: At Dscout , we’re building the most flexible and powerful UX research platform on the market—trusted by the world’s top brands in finance (JP Morgan Chase, Intuit, Charles Schwab, PayPal), healthcare (Aya, Headspace), consumer goods (Keen, Verizon, Target, Northface), and tech (Google, Amazon, Facebook, Meta, Spotify, AirBnB). Our tools help teams deeply understand the humans behind their products, so they can build better ones. We are expanding our smart and driven team and would love for you to join us. At Dscout, we're building the human-grounded layer that teaches AI to work in the real world and proves it stays aligned there. We are expanding our smart and driven team and would love for you to join us. Dscout AI Training & Evals builds human data and evals that show whether AI works for real people. For ten years Dscout has captured how people behave in real context, with consent and scientific rigor. Dscout AI Training & Evals points that engine at AI: consented human behavior and judgment, turned into the training data, evals, and benchmarks AI teams trust. Models ace benchmarks and still surprise people in the wild. A benchmark says how capable a model is. It does not say whether the model works for the person using it, across weeks, in the mess of real life. That gap is where we work. We serve AI researchers, the product builders who ship alongside them, and the research teams who partner with both. We are a new unit inside an established company: live customers, a mature platform (React, Elixir, Python, Swift, Kotlin; SOC 2 and HITRUST certified), a small senior team, and room to build. Our customers need a partner who can design the answer, build it, and ship it fast. Ground Truth sits where deployment meets research: what we learn in the field shapes the science, and the science shapes what we ship. Come build it with us. Why this seat Work on a problem the field has not solved: measuring whether AI works for real people, over real time. Study something most evals do not have: real participants, doing real tasks in their own context. Own the benchmark. You are founding it, not joining a team that has one. Publish. Methods and benchmarks go to the research community, with first authorship on the benchmark. Join a small senior team with direct access to the Head of AI Research and the GM. This is a research-first role focused on questions where the right rubric, benchmark, or method does not yet exist. Build quality signals that put evidence behind every data point we ship. Long-horizon, real-user benchmarks Design Dscout’s first benchmark: real users, in real context, over long horizons. Multi-week tasks across tools, not one-shot prompts. Define the protocol, task design, scoring, and release. Work with our delivery team on fieldwork. Work out how to keep a living benchmark honest over time: drift, contamination, difficulty, and what counts as a meaningful change. Write the paper and own the public release. Human judgment as training and eval signal Study when real-world human feedback improves a model and when it adds noise. Explore how preference and judgment data from representative people differ from expert data. Turn findings into methods our forward deployed engineers and delivery team can run in the field. New research directions These areas are the core, not the whole list. You will have significant latitude to propose new programs, such as calibrating user simulations against real behavior, human-AI collaboration, and behavioral evaluation of agents. Co-author with outside labs and academics on studies that need real-user data. Help run our paper-reading group. A good first year A QA and rubric framework running on live customer programs, with documented validity. Benchmark v0 released, with a paper submitted to a top venue. At least one external team using or citing our work. Delivery colleagues using your methods without needing you in the room. How we will hire: a conversation with the Head of AI Research; a research talk on your publication; a design exercise (how would you validate a rubric for a long-horizon task?); a conversation with the GM, forward deployed engineers, and delivery partners. What we care about most. A strong publication record helps. We care most about whether you can find the question that matters, design a rigorous way to answer it, and move fast enough that the answer is still useful. About the Company Our client is a Series B enterprise AI startup that raised $108M from a16z, Benchmark, First Round, BoxGroup, and YC, building infrastructure that turns complex documents into structured, AI-ready data. Its API-based platform processes PDFs, images, spreadsheets, and other unstructured files, helping organizations build production AI applications and automate document-intensive workflows. Our client supports AI-native startups and large enterprises with demanding accuracy and deployment requirements. The team is founder-led and engineering-first, with engineers working directly with customers and using what they learn to improve the product. The Mission Make complex document data reliable enough to build on. Our client helps organizations unlock information inside unstructured files while preserving the detail and structure that downstream applications depend on. The goal is to deliver accurate, usable data that holds up in production, not simply extract text that looks convincing in a demo. jobs.title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer, Personalization
jobs.jd: The Personalization team makes deciding what to play next easier and more enjoyable for every listener. From Blend to Discover Weekly, we’re behind some of Spotify ’s most-loved features. We built them by understanding the world of music and podcasts better than anyone else. Join us and you’ll keep millions of users listening by making great recommendations to each and every one of them. Growlithe is a fast-moving squad within Spotify's Conversation Product Area, focused on bringing emerging Search and agentic experiences to life. We explore, define, build, validate, and optimize new ideas to help listeners discover the content they love. Our work spans personalized Search, music video discovery and ranking, audiobook Search expansion, and the foundations of more social Search experiences. We're looking for a Senior Machine Learning Engineer to help shape the next generation of Search at Spotify. You'll work at the intersection of machine learning, personalization, and product development, turning complex challenges into intuitive discovery experiences for millions of listeners. What You'll Do Build and improve machine learning models that make Spotify Search more relevant, personalized, and engaging for listeners. Develop and optimize ranking and backend retrieval systems that help listeners discover music, videos, audiobooks, and other content. Explore emerging AI and agentic approaches to create more intuitive and conversational Search experiences. Design, implement, and evaluate machine learning solutions, taking ideas from early experimentation through production. Partner with engineers, product managers, designers, and researchers to identify opportunities and deliver meaningful improvements to Search. Use experimentation, data analysis, and performance metrics to understand model behavior, validate hypotheses, and improve the listener experience. Contribute to scalable machine learning infrastructure and engineering practices that support reliable, high-quality Search experiences. Share knowledge, challenge assumptions constructively, and help shape the technical direction of machine learning within the squad. Who You Are You have experience building, deploying, and improving machine learning systems in production environments. You have a strong understanding of machine learning approaches for information retrieval, search ranking, recommendation systems, or personalization. You are proficient in Python and comfortable working with modern machine learning frameworks and data processing tools. You have experience and a desire to lean into backend engineering at Spotify scale. You understand how to design and evaluate experiments, interpret model performance, and translate technical findings into product improvements. You have experience working with large-scale datasets and understand the challenges of building reliable, scalable machine learning systems. You are curious about emerging AI technologies, including large language models and agentic systems, and interested in their potential to improve discovery experiences. You enjoy working across disciplines, communicating technical ideas clearly, and learning from different perspectives. You are comfortable navigating ambiguity, taking ownership of complex challenges, and balancing experimentation with practical delivery. Where You'll Be This role is based in Eastern Standard Time We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home. Compensation Additional Information The United States base range for this position is 184,049–262,928 USD, plus equity. The benefits available for this position include health insurance, six-month paid parental leave, 401(k) retirement plan, monthly meal allowance, 23 paid days off, paid flexible holidays, and paid sick leave. These ranges may be modified in the future. Spotify is an equal opportunity employer. You are welcome at Spotify for who you are, no matter where you come from, what you look like, or what’s playing in your headphones. Our platform is for everyone, and so is our workplace. The more voices we have represented and amplified in our business, the more we will all thrive, contribute, and be forward-thinking! So bring us your personal experience, your perspectives, and your background. It’s in our differences that we will find the power to keep revolutionizing the way the world listens. At Spotify, we are passionate about inclusivity and making sure our entire recruitment process is accessible to everyone. We have ways to request reasonable accommodations during the interview process and help assist in what you need. If you need accommodations at any stage of the application or interview process, please let us know - we’re here to support you in any way we can.

jobs.title: Data Scientist, FX Quantitative Research
jobs.jd:
Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world's largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

Data Science at Stripe is a vibrant community where data scientists and data analysts learn and grow together. The Treasury Finance Data Science team builds the models, risk frameworks, and decision tools behind how Stripe manages money at global scale: liquidity, funding, counterparty risk, and foreign exchange.

Stripe moves funds across 135+ currencies every day. That creates FX exposure from merchant flows, multi-currency balances, and entity funding. In this role, you'll be a thought partner and builder alongside Stripe's FX team. Together you'll develop the quantitative foundation for how Stripe measures, forecasts, and hedges FX exposure.

What you'll do

You'll be the senior quantitative lead for FX within Treasury Finance Data Science. You'll co-build with Treasury, the FX hedging team, Finance, and Engineering: shaping the research agenda, turning ideas into rigorous models, and building the systems that put those models to work. Data Science owns these systems. They produce the decision-critical outputs and analyses that the FX team and Treasury leadership rely on. This is a hands-on role. You'll design the methodology, write the code, and ship it into production.

Responsibilities

  • Partner with the FX team to build and evolve FX risk measurement: exposure aggregation across entities and currencies, VaR / Expected Shortfall, stress testing, and scenario analysis
  • Develop forecasting models for FX exposures and multi-currency cash flows. Quantify forecast uncertainty so it can inform hedge sizing and timing.
  • Co-design hedge optimization and decision frameworks with the FX team that weigh hedge cost, residual risk, P&L volatility, and liquidity constraints
  • Build ML and statistical systems for trading and risk (signal research, anomaly detection on flows, execution and cost analytics), and take them from prototype to production
  • Own the production systems that generate decision-critical FX outputs, partnering with Engineering on reliability, SLAs, monitoring, alerting, and incident response for risk-critical workflows
  • Partner deeply with Treasury Finance stakeholders to turn business questions into quantitative frameworks. Anticipate needs and help shape FX risk strategy rather than reacting to requests.
  • Produce clear, trusted analyses and reporting that inform Treasury and Finance leadership decisions, including leadership-level reporting such as MBRs and QBRs
  • Use AI tools (code assistants, LLM-based agents) to speed up modeling, analysis, and automation, while maintaining rigor, validation, and auditability
  • Raise the technical bar for FX quantitative work within Data Science: methodology standards, model validation, documentation, and mentoring other data scientists

Who you are

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

  • BS/BA with 8+ years, MS/MA with 6+ years, or PhD with 3+ years of full-time experience in quantitative finance, risk modeling, quantitative research, or data science
  • Hands-on quantitative experience at a bank, asset manager, hedge fund, trading firm, or similar financial institution, with direct exposure to FX, rates, or market risk
  • Strong foundation in statistics, probability, and time-series modeling, plus working knowledge of risk measures (VaR, Expected Shortfall, stress testing) and hedging instruments (forwards, swaps, options)
  • Proficiency in Python and SQL. You write production-quality code, not just research scripts.
  • Experience taking models or analytical systems from research into production
  • Business acumen and the ability to turn complex analyses into clear, decision-ready insights
  • Ability to clearly communicate results and drive impact with cross-functional partners, including senior non-technical stakeholders
  • Ability to manage multiple projects at once, with strong attention to detail
  • Experience using AI tools to speed up modeling, analysis, and coding

Preferred qualifications

  • MS or PhD in a quantitative field (e.g., Quantitative / Mathematical Finance, Financial Engineering, Statistics, Mathematics, Physics, Computer Science, Economics, Operations Research)
  • Applied machine learning experience in trading or risk (e.g., forecasting, execution analytics, signal research, anomaly detection)
  • Experience with corporate treasury or balance-sheet FX: multi-entity exposure management, hedge programs, and treasury concepts such as liquidity, funding, and cash positioning
  • Experience building risk or decision systems with engineering standards: code review, testing, monitoring, and defined SLAs
  • Experience with distributed data tools (e.g., Spark) and workflow orchestration (e.g., Airflow, Flyte)
  • Prior experience at a growth-stage internet, fintech, or payments company
  • Experience creating leadership-level reporting, such as QBRs and MBRs
  • A builder's mindset, with a willingness to question assumptions and conventional wisdom
  • Interest in how data products enable automated a

Our mission is to help organizations move AI workflows cleanly into production through two main paths: creating reusable software architectures that solve common industry problems, and contributing code directly to upstream open-source projects to fix enterprise gaps in system deployment, runtime tuning, and platform management. Basing our engineering team in Singapore creates a close feedback loop between customers, partners, and core product teams. This direct connection keeps our development roadmaps relevant, speeds up solution delivery, and strengthens our ability to co-innovate across the region. Role Overview The Senior AI/ML Engineer is a highly technical, hands-on role at the intersection of Enterprise AI and client-facing architecture. As part of our Customer Engineering function, you will write production-grade solution blueprints alongside strategic customers and technology partners. Your mission is to solve immediate, high-stakes operational bottlenecks in the APAC region by delivering repeatable, extensible, and open-sourced AI Quickstarts that show the industry how to solve complex challenges. In this team, career growth and seniority are defined purely by your technical competence, architectural depth, and ability to deliver end-to-end solutions autonomously in highly ambiguous environments. There is no expectation of team management, project coordination, or formal talent mentorship; your progression is driven entirely by engineering impact. What You Will Do: Enterprise-Minded Blueprinting: Design and build comprehensive, production-ready architecture blueprints and reference codebases. These blueprints must naturally take into account critical enterprise requirements—including systems-level hardening, infrastructure scalability, and network isolation boundaries—without you needing to perform the last-mile hands-on production deployment yourself. Open-Source AI Quickstarts: Package repeatable, extensible technical architectures as open-sourced AI Quickstarts to solve complex, real-world industry problems and accelerate ecosystem adoption. Co-Development & Integration: Collaborate with external engineering teams (such as semiconductor partners, regional AI programs, and software vendors) to validate joint-architecture blueprints, ensuring stable integrations across the system stack. Benchmarking & Evaluation: Design and integrate automated testing, evaluation harnesses, and system-level telemetry into blueprints to monitor and measure performance metrics like latency, throughput, cost, and model quality. Regulated & Secure Design: Proactively incorporate robust data privacy standards, secure network perimeters, and localized hosting considerations into all solution blueprints to satisfy compliance and risk management requirements in highly regulated environments. What You Will Bring: Academic & Professional Experience Education: Bachelor’s or Master's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related quantitative field. Software Engineering Foundations: Excellent understanding of software engineering fundamentals, including clean code principles, test-driven development (TDD), CI/CD automation pipelines, and version control (Git) workflows. Communication: Clear verbal and written communication skills in English, with the ability to articulate complex technical architectures to other engineers and technical stakeholders. Core Technical Stack Programming Languages: Exceptional, hands-on proficiency in Python (specifically for machine learning and systems programming). Solid familiarity with lower-level system languages such as Go or C/C++ is highly preferred. Deep Learning & ML Libraries: Strong familiarity with PyTorch and core NLP/vision ecosystems (e.g., Hugging Face Transformers , datasets, and tokenizers). Cloud-Native Frameworks: Strong practical experience deploying containerized applications on Kubernetes or production-grade enterprise container orchestration platforms. Base MLOps Knowledge: Conceptual and hands-on understanding of model serving lifecycles, data ingestion steps, and automated packaging. Target Knowledge Domains & Growth Areas We are building a multi-disciplinary engineering squad. Candidates are expected to bring experience in some of the following domains, and will have the opportunity to continuously develop their skills across all of them as they grow in seniority: Platform & Pipeline Engineering: Experience with distributed computing frameworks and cluster schedulers (such as Ray ), workflow orchestration (such as MLflow or Kubeflow ), distributed unstructured data parsing tools (such as Docling ), and vector database structures. Generative AI & Agentic Architectures: Familiarity with LLM orchestration engines (such as LangChain , LlamaIndex , or LangGraph ), agentic workflows (AgentOps), tool-calling protocols (such as Model Context Protocol ) and model fine-tuning (PEFT/SFT). Hardware Heterogeneity & Runtime Optimization: Understanding of model serving runtimes (such as vLLM ), optimizing engines for latency and throughput (e.g., KV cache offloading, chunked prefill), and running benchmarks across diverse hardware setups including CUDA, ROCm, and emerging GPU/NPU architectures. Regulated Deployments: Designing isolated, air-gapped container networks, secure registry services, and local inference environments to meet strict data residency, privacy, and compliance policies. Nice-to-Have: Industry Domain Experience While not strictly required, experience applying AI/ML architectures to solve challenges in the following regulated industries is a strong advantage: Financial Services (FSI): Familiarity with risk-assessment models, fraud detection patterns, or compliance requirements under regulatory frameworks.
